amendment: Initial training was interrupted before endpoint DEV evaluation to hold menu order fixed within each contract counterfactual pair. Wording, labels and training recipe were unchanged; the final baseline is remeasured before restarting from the released adapter. See menu-correction.json.

rules.S1: Route to the apparent primary topic: revenue, identity, reliability, developer.

inference_information: Messages, contract code, priority, desk names and a generic internal-policy instruction. The actual C7 mapping is intentionally learned from labels, not printed in the prompt.
split_design: Separately authored dev messages; no message string/template substitution crosses train/dev. Both contract counterfactuals stay in the same message group/split and use IDENTICAL menus. Only contract code changes within a pair. Menu order rotates by message index, not contract or target. Includes primary-topic hard negatives.
baseline_runtime: PyTorch BF16 released adapter, before any adaptation
headroom_admission: Use the corrected candidate if released-model dev accuracy is between 0.3 and 0.75; record it before final training. No endpoint-quality-based dataset or checkpoint selection.
evaluation: Compare released versus endpoint in the same BF16 runtime on all 64 user DEV and all 24 authored retention DEV rows. Report per-contract results and paired before/after probabilities.
export: Reload adapter on BF16 base, merge, convert/quantize Q4_K_M, compare all 64 dev decisions on CPU GGUF, serve the artifact with the public HTTP server.
caveat: A fictional policy-learning demonstration, not evidence that fine-tuning beats putting known rules into code or explicit instructions. No broad capability claim.
gpu_target: A physically rented 24 GB RTX A5000
